actual_tools: public KN035 literature and structural records
execution.implementation: literature-backed orthogonal assay design and deterministic 96-well allocation; no wet-lab or pricing execution

observations: The open-access KN035 study documents ELISA, BLI, and flow-cytometry methods relevant to PD-L1 nanobody evaluation.
The generated plate map assigns 96 unique wells: 72 candidate-dose wells and 24 control wells.
The assay plan contains five Boltz-prioritized variants plus the KN035 parent and explicitly records that no wet-lab experiment or vendor quote occurred.
A genuine Rosalind launcher call returned ready=true but performed no assay design, pricing, purchasing, or wet-lab work.
interpretation: Sequential sample-quality, direct-binding, competition, and cell-surface assays provide orthogonal evidence for candidate selection.
Published KN035 measurements motivate assay choice but cannot be assigned to untested variants.
limitations: The output is an experimental plan and contains no measured affinity, inhibition, expression, stability, or specificity result.
The proposed BLI concentrations and immobilization format require pilot optimization.
No complete purchasing price is reported because no vendor quotes were collected.

provenance.note: Published assay modes inform the proposed experiment sequence; the builder creates the candidate allocation and complete plate map without asserting an experimental result. The Rosalind observation records chooser readiness only.

reproduction: Read and verify the cited KN035 methods in the public evidence note.
Run python build_case.py and verify 96 unique plate wells.
Adapt the proposed parameters to the available protein formats and instruments before laboratory use.
